chapter: Kansas City, Omaha and Lloyd Hunter
title: The six-piece band in Omaha, taking Jo Jones's job
summary: In Omaha he took Jo Jones's job in a six-piece band with Floyd Smith, Jimmy Keith and Paul King, lodging with Dave Henderson.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: Yeah. Oh, that's terrific. Well, anyway, so Jo said -- so right away he thought he'd put you in in Omaha, in his place?
That's what he did, he really did.
And they kept on playing -- that was with Andy Kirk.
What's Floyd's last name? Floyd Smith.
Floyd Smith, myself and the bass player. They called him Basie. I can't think of his name.
Yeah, didn't he play in a band that Charlie Parker was in, too?
He played in Harlan Leonard's band.
And they had someone else, had, I think, a trumpet player.
It was piano and bass, guitar, drums, tenor player and -- who was the trumpet player? I think it was Paul King. It was, Paul King played trumpet.
Oh, yeah, very good trumpet player.
Did you play with them afterwards anywhere?
Well, I had played with them in a
Oh, yeah. Who was the -- oh, yeah, Jimmy Keith, yeah.
Yeah. They had a good band.
Yeah, it was a good six-piece band.
I should think that was a big thrill for you, the first time you played -- were playing steadily in a small band.
First time I'd been out of town by myself.
Did you take a room or something?
You took a room or something to stay in?
Oh, yes, we had rooms when we got there.
And Jo Jones had told us where we could get a room.
And a fellow named Dave Henderson, --
We all called him Dry Hat.
Yeah, it was a funny name.
Yeah. And he was a short guy, real dark, very beautiful hair.
And he had the house, and we all had rooms there.
So I stayed there with the band until -- oh, for about three months. And then I left the band and joined Floyd Hunter's band.
